_doc: Canonical trade identity, availability and training time. training_years is the years of apprenticeship or schooling before a person is productive in the trade (an estimate of the skill, not a wage); a trade that states none takes its family's median. Wages are not stored here: sim/labour/wages.py derives them. fatality_risk_per_year is the yearly chance a worker of the trade dies at work, with fatality_source and fatality_confidence; the economy raises the wage asked for a trade by it. literate marks a trade whose practice is reading and writing, so literacy caps how many there are; taught_from is the trade a new one is taught from by default; tool_basket lists the materials a self-equipped worker replaces to stay in the trade; staff_resource names the generic staffing resource a trade fills. These four are labelled heuristics (confidence D) of the engine's labour model, moved here from code.

miner.fatality_source: Royal Commission and Mines Inspectorate returns for British coal mining in the mid nineteenth century give deaths of roughly three to five per thousand miners a year (Church, History of the British Coal Industry, vol. 3; Duckham 1973); pre-industrial mining is taken as no safer.

soldier.note: A man under arms, drawn from the working age; the state's army is booked in this trade. Basic training is months, not years (Vegetius, De re militari 1.13 gives four months).
soldier.fatality_source: Pre-industrial armies lost a few per cent of their men a year, most to disease and some to battle (Parker, The Military Revolution; Scheidel on Roman military mortality). An order of magnitude averaged over peace and war, not a measured rate.
